verdict: Duke Energy grew revenue 7% to $9.1B and earned $1.55B for common shareholders — EPS of $1.99 — as it recovered the cost of new infrastructure from customers and got help from favorable weather.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Reported and adjusted EPS were the same — no special items

segments.name: Regulated electric
segments.note: Selling electricity in the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky at prices set by regulators. Up 7% as Duke recovered infrastructure spending in rates and weather was favorable. This segment earned $1,817M.

segments.name: Regulated natural gas
segments.note: Gas distribution (Piedmont Natural Gas). Revenue was flat in this seasonally quiet quarter for heating, and the segment lost $19M, as usual outside winter.

segments.name: Nonregulated electric & other
segments.note: Small non-regulated activities outside the utilities — under 1% of revenue.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of plants, grids and pipelines over their long lives — a non-cash charge that rises as Duke builds.

opex.name: Operation, maintenance & other
opex.note: Running and repairing the grid and plants, and serving customers day to day.

opex.name: Property & other taxes
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on power plants and networks.

opex.name: Asset-sale gains & other, net
opex.note: A small net credit: $11M of gains on selling other assets plus a $2M net impairment credit (so it reduces expenses).

otherDetail: Other expense of $897M, net: $967M of interest expense, partly offset by $147M of other income and $22M of equity earnings from part-owned affiliates — and it also includes $85M of profit belonging to noncontrolling partners and $14M of preferred dividends, so the flow lands on the $1,551M available to common shareholders.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel used in generation plus purchased power ($2,738M) and the cost of natural gas bought for customers ($117M) are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror Duke's income statement. Net income here is the $1,551M available to common stockholders (after $85M for noncontrolling interests and $14M of preferred dividends on total net income of $1,650M), matching the $1.99 EPS.

takeaways.title: Electric utilities carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure earned $1,817M, up 10% from $1,658M, driven by recovering infrastructure investment in customer rates and favorable weather. Gas lost $19M in its off-season and Other lost $247M.

takeaways.title: A clean quarter, guidance raised
takeaways.text: Reported EPS of $1.99 exactly matched adjusted EPS — there were no special items to strip out. Duke narrowed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70–$6.80, toward the top of its range.

takeaways.title: A record building program
takeaways.text: Duke is executing a record generation build to add 16 gigawatts of capacity by 2031 — roughly 16 large power plants' worth — to serve fast-growing states. Depreciation ($1,709M) and interest ($967M) already reflect the growing asset base.
